# Papers still wanted

DOIs checked against Crossref on 2026-09-28 (title match confirmed). Order
reflects relevance to the open questions in `huygens/REPORT.md`.

## 1. Navigation and altitude (the tilt result depends on these)
| paper | why | DOI |
|---|---|---|
| Kazeminejad et al. 2007, PSS 55. Huygens' entry and descent through Titan's atmosphere: methodology and results of the trajectory reconstruction | source of the App. 3 altitudes (DTWG); their stated errors | https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pss.2007.04.013 |
| Kazeminejad et al. 2011, Adv. Space Res. 47. Titan's new pole: implications for the Huygens entry and descent trajectory and landing coordinates | later trajectory revision (DTWG#5) used by Karkoschka 2016 | https://doi.org/10.1016/j.asr.2011.01.019 |
| Fulchignoni et al. 2005, Nature 438. In situ measurements of the physical characteristics of Titan's environment | HASI pressure/temperature profile behind the altitudes | https://doi.org/10.1038/nature04314 |
| Bird et al. 2005, Nature 438. The vertical profile of winds on Titan | Doppler zonal winds; fixes Karkoschka's east-west tilt | https://doi.org/10.1038/nature04060 |

## 2. DISR imaging and the landing site
| paper | why | DOI |
|---|---|---|
| Tomasko et al. 2005, Nature 438. Rain, winds and haze during the Huygens probe's descent to Titan's surface | first DISR results and first stereo topography | https://doi.org/10.1038/nature04126 |
| Tomasko et al. 2002, Space Sci. Rev. 104. The DISR experiment on the Huygens entry probe of Titan | instrument definition (cameras, geometry) | https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1023632422098 |
| Lebreton et al. 2005, Nature 438. An overview of the descent and landing of the Huygens probe on Titan | mission timeline and attitude context | https://doi.org/10.1038/nature04347 |
| Keller et al. 2008, PSS 56. The properties of Titan's surface at the Huygens landing site from DISR observations | photometry; K&S 2016 dispute its phase-function reading | https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pss.2007.11.020 |
| Schröder & Keller 2008, PSS 56. The reflectance spectrum of Titan's surface at the Huygens landing site determined by DISR | surface photometry | https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pss.2007.10.011 |
| Schröder et al. 2012, PSS 73. Bouncing on Titan: motion of the Huygens probe in the seconds after landing | landing geometry cited by Karkoschka 2016 | https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pss.2012.08.007 |
| Soderblom, L.A. et al. 2007, PSS 55. Correlations between Cassini VIMS spectra and RADAR SAR images: implications for Titan's surface composition and the character of the Huygens probe landing site | regional context, RADAR tie to the DISR mosaic | https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pss.2007.04.014 |

## 3. IPGP's tilt method (river routing)
| paper | why | DOI |
|---|---|---|
| Perron et al. 2006, JGR 111. Valley formation and methane precipitation rates on Titan | drainage interpretation of the landing site | https://doi.org/10.1029/2005JE002602 |
| Burr et al. 2013, GSA Bulletin 125. Fluvial features on Titan: insights from morphology and modeling | river-network reasoning used for the tilt | https://doi.org/10.1130/B30612.1 |
| Tarboton 1997, Water Resour. Res. 33. A new method for the determination of flow directions and upslope areas in grid DEMs | the routing algorithm (D-infinity) | https://doi.org/10.1029/96WR03137 |
| Schwanghart & Scherler 2014, Earth Surf. Dynam. 2. TopoToolbox 2 (open access) | software IPGP used | https://doi.org/10.5194/esurf-2-1-2014 |

## Items without a DOI
- Daudon et al. 2020 supporting information (Figures S5-S8: raw tilt, routing
  score grid, USGS re-tilt). Wiley supplementary file on the article page.
- Archinal et al. 2006, "Photogrammetric analysis of Huygens DISR images of
  Titan", ISPRS proceedings (USGS method details).
- ESA SPICE Service 2019, Huygens operational SPICE kernels (dataset):
  https://doi.org/10.5270/esa-ssem3np (resolves). Needed to compare IPGP's
  attitude with App. 3.
